method: Projection-loss and qualification-fixture outcomes were frozen in artifacts/operability.v2.blind-reviewer2.precompare.json before authored permittedLoss values, fixture validity, or checker logic were read.
The gate inventory was traced to its alleged subjects and targets, rather than accepting gate names as coverage.
Identity, budget, audit, and projection statements were compared across sections for contradictory global claims.
Temporary invalid mutations were used to audit what check-operability.py actually protects.

blindComparison.qualificationFixtures: All seven fixture outcomes matched the independent derivation.

projectionParity.reviewerPermittedLoss: everything except the total termination class encoded by the process status
inline detail only when omitted count, visible truncation, and exact retrieval route are present
none; namespaced property bags can preserve Coverage and other OpenSIP fields
presentation only; pagination must preserve reachability and continuation truth

blindComparison.sarifEvidence: SARIF 2.1.0 property bags support additional named properties, so absence of a native display field does not make Coverage semantically unrepresentable: https://docs.oasis-open.org/sarif/sarif/v2.1.0/os/sarif-v2.1.0-os.html
blindComparison.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A target interoperability requirement that forbids SARIF property bags and explicitly chooses a lossy export, in which case the surface must not be advertised as parity-preserving.

checkerMutationAudit.mutation: Delete G1 through G11, leaving only G12
Replace projection requiredFields with five unrelated strings
Set G12 target to an imaginary checker
Delete OP-05, the projection conformance declaration

findings.evidence: gateQualification.releaseRule blocks release while any required property lacks a qualified gate, but this artifact defines neither the complete required-property set nor a property-to-gate relation. check-operability.py permits deletion of G1 through G11 and still passes. Only G7 carries blocking:true, and that field is itself unchecked.
findings.impact: The release decision is not computable. Implementations may silently omit a required property or gate and obtain a greener release posture merely by deleting the record.
findings.requiredChange: Define a closed RequiredProperty schema and an exhaustive property-to-one-or-more-gates map, including source claim and subject. Derive a typed release decision from that map. The checker must reject an omitted required property, missing gate, wrong subject, or removed blocking obligation.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A referenced binding artifact that supplies an exhaustive required-property set and a checker that joins it to every gate and computes the release decision.

findings.evidence: observability.correlation requires ExecutionId on every event in every plane, while identityDomain says pre-admission events carry only RequestId and ExecutionId appears after attempt admission. observability.volumeBudgets requires per-Run budgets on every non-evidence plane, while identityDomain says budgeting is by request/execution and 'Never universally by Run — a Run may not exist.'
findings.impact: No implementation can satisfy both halves. Pre-admission validation diagnostics either invent nonexistent identities and budgets or violate the observability rules.
findings.requiredChange: Make correlation and budgets phase-aware: RequestId always; ExecutionId only after attempt admission; RunId only after seal. Budget by RequestId before admission, ExecutionId after admission, and optionally RunId after seal. Add pre-admission rejection and post-seal event fixtures.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A binding definition that restricts 'every event' and 'per-Run' to post-admission/post-seal events, though the current prose contains no such restriction.

findings.evidence: G12 is marked QUALIFIED with target 'the eight checkers', although the final prompt names twelve retained checkers plus completeness. observedFailure is a bare true value with no retained execution/evidence identity, and check-operability.py neither invokes those checkers nor validates the target. An imaginary target passes. The broad discharged property 'the architecture is internally coherent' exceeds what local schema checkers can establish.
findings.impact: A stale, self-attested gate discharges a global architecture claim. Green local consistency checks can coexist with wrong framing and semantic contradictions, as the recorded error history demonstrates.
findings.requiredChange: Change G12's property to the narrow checker claim, enumerate exact checker identities/versions and mutation results, retain an execution record, and make a meta-runner invoke them. Do not use G12 to discharge semantic or framing coherence. Update the register's stale title 'thirteen release gates' to twelve or restore the missing gate intentionally.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A retained meta-run binding the exact final checker set and negative controls, plus an independently justified definition under which 'internally coherent' means only schema consistency.

findings.evidence: projectionParity is free-form prose. The checker accepts arbitrary required-field names and a human surface that loses everything silently. OP-05 merely declares that a future canonical Run is projected; no canonical Run or per-field expected projection is present. The authored SARIF loss is also unnecessary because SARIF property bags can carry custom Coverage fields.
findings.impact: Five outputs can disagree on verdict, identity, Coverage, or truncation while the architecture checker stays green. Agents and CI could see materially different truth from humans.
findings.requiredChange: Define typed per-surface projection schemas and one canonical Run corpus spanning pass/fail/indeterminate, truncation, artifacts, and IDs. Derive each projection and compare fields mechanically. Preserve Coverage in SARIF namespaced properties; test both serialized retention and consumer-visible fallback behavior.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: Executable projection goldens that reject each recorded loss mutation and a documented target restriction proving SARIF extensions cannot be used.

findings.evidence: G9 is correctly UNQUALIFIED-NO-TARGET because capability denial needs ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT. G10, however, describes closure analysis over the built core and can target a build artifact now; its runtime-denial half should be a separate gate. G11 can target an orchestration host plus deliberately faulting provider without waiting for a capability-restricted runtime. The artifact labels all three targetless.
findings.impact: Real, buildable checks are deferred behind an unrelated reopened mechanism. 'No target' becomes defeatism rather than an honest account of what can be tested.
findings.requiredChange: Keep runtime capability denial targetless; split static core-closure and runtime denial; give static closure a built-package target; give process fault containment a host/provider fault-injection target. Reserve UNQUALIFIED-NO-TARGET only for mechanisms that genuinely do not exist in the selected architecture.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A dependency showing that the selected host cannot execute or isolate a faulting provider at all without the same restricted runtime, or that no core build artifact exists to inspect.

findings.evidence: auditPlane is a paragraph and field list, not a typed record or write protocol. It does not define canonical before/after commitments, actor identity, atomicity relative to the mutation, audit-write failure behavior, ordering, concurrency, or redaction. OP-06 only states a future assertion.
findings.impact: A mutation can succeed without a durable audit record, or an audit record can claim a mutation that rolled back. Different hosts can emit incompatible records while all architecture checks pass.
findings.requiredChange: Specify a HostAuditRecord union and transaction protocol with required IDs, canonical commitments, privacy classes, ordering, failure semantics, and mutation/audit atomicity. Add crash-before, crash-after, concurrent mutation, rollback, purge, and redaction goldens.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A referenced binding host-audit schema and atomic protocol elsewhere in the artifact set.

findings.evidence: G7's target depends on a 'declared reference capacity class', but knownLimitations admits that class is unspecified. The gate combines memory, disk, runtime, and cancellation without thresholds or platform/workload dimensions.
findings.impact: A catastrophic resource regression has no falsifiable boundary even though G7 is the only explicitly blocking gate.
findings.requiredChange: Define versioned capacity classes with repository shape, language mix, hardware floor, maximum memory/disk/runtime, cancellation deadline, and measurement protocol. Split independently actionable resource dimensions if one aggregate result would hide failures.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A binding capacity-class artifact already referenced by G7.

adjudication.elevenUnqualified: Correct for product release: an implementation guarantee should not be published until its positive and negative controls have actually run. This is not a reason to reject a greenfield architecture by itself. It becomes an architecture blocker only where the gate domain or target is undefined, as in R2-OP-01, R2-OP-05, and R2-OP-07.
adjudication.observedFailure: The right qualification bar, provided the observed failure is a retained, reproducible evidence record rather than a boolean assertion.

sealedPropertiesCovered: projection parity across machine, exit, human, SARIF, and agent surfaces
release properties have qualified implementation gates
knownLimitations: No implementation exists, so this review distinguishes an architecture-complete gate definition from a product-qualified gate result.
SARIF display behavior varies by consumer; the claim here is that the serialized interchange need not lose the data.
No claim-register status was changed: OPERABILITY is already CANDIDATE.

sealRecommendation.blocker: The release rule has no exhaustive required-property mapping, the event identity/budget rules contradict each other, and projection parity is not executable.
